message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"1.17","text":"I also set out my purpose from the beginning, how I had exhausted myself in inquiries with no way through, and everything I had disclosed to you at the outset, so that I need not write the same things again. I said, “I am quite ready to accompany you—for I do not know how it is that I gladly desire this. Yet I first want to be fully assured about the truth, so that I may know whether the soul happens to be mortal or is immortal; and, if it is eternal, whether it is to be judged for what it has done here; whether there is, after all, anything just or pleasing to God; whether the world has come into being and why it came into being; whether it will not be dissolved and whether it will be dissolved; and whether it will be better or will not even exist. And, not to speak category by category, I said that I wanted to learn both these things and what follows from them.” He answered this: “In brief, Clement, I will provide you with knowledge of realities; and now hear from it the matters at hand.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"εἰς ζητήσεις ἀπόρους ἐκενώθην","chosen":"I had exhausted myself in inquiries with no way through","rationale":"Preserves the image of being emptied or spent and the lack of a way to resolve the inquiries."},{"source_quote":"τοῦτο γὰρ οὐκ οἶδα ὅπως χαίρων θέλω","chosen":"for I do not know how it is that I gladly desire this","rationale":"Retains the unusual claim of an unexplained yet glad desire rather than reducing it to simple willingness."},{"source_quote":"εἰ οὐ λυθήσεται καὶ εἰ λυθήσεται","chosen":"whether it will not be dissolved and whether it will be dissolved","rationale":"Preserves both alternatives, including the first clause’s explicit negation."},{"source_quote":"τὴν τῶν ὄντων γνῶσιν","chosen":"knowledge of realities","rationale":"Renders τὰ ὄντα as the things that exist without imposing a more specialized metaphysical formulation."},{"source_quote":"καὶ τὰ νῦν ἐξ αὐτῆς ἄκουσον","chosen":"and now hear from it the matters at hand","rationale":"Takes αὐτῆς as referring to the promised knowledge and τὰ νῦν as what is presently relevant."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.18","text":"The counsel of God has become hidden in many ways. The first things are bad initiation, wicked upbringing, grievous habituation, unwholesome association, and incorrect preconception. Because of these come error, then absence of fear, unbelief, sexual immorality, love of money, vainglory, and countless other such evils. Like a mass of smoke inhabiting the world as one house, this multitude clouded the sight of the men living within and did not allow them to look up and, from the design, discern the God who created it and recognize what seems good to him. Therefore lovers of truth must cry out from deep within their breasts and summon assistance with truth-loving reasoning, so that someone who is outside the smoke-filled house may approach and open a door, in order that the sunlight outside may be admitted into the house and the smoke of the fire, being inside, may be expelled.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἡ τοῦ θεοῦ βουλὴ ἐν ἀδήλῳ γέγονεν","chosen":"The counsel of God has become hidden","rationale":"Conveys the resulting state of obscurity expressed by ἐν ἀδήλῳ and γέγονεν."},{"source_quote":"εἰσαγωγὴ κακή, συντροφία πονηρά, συνήθεια δεινή, ὁμιλία οὐ καλή, πρόληψις οὐκ ὀρθή","chosen":"bad initiation, wicked upbringing, grievous habituation, unwholesome association, and incorrect preconception","rationale":"Keeps the sequence of initial formation, upbringing, acquired habit, association, and prior assumption distinct."},{"source_quote":"ἀφοβία","chosen":"absence of fear","rationale":"Avoids the favorable connotations of “fearlessness” without supplying an unstated object of fear."},{"source_quote":"ἀναβλέψαντας ἐκ τῆς διαγραφῆς τὸν δημιουργήσαντα νοῆσαι θεὸν","chosen":"to look up and, from the design, discern the God who created it","rationale":"Treats the delineated order as the basis from which its creator may be discerned."},{"source_quote":"ὁ δὲ ἐντὸς τοῦ πυρὸς ὢν ἐκβληθῆναι καπνός","chosen":"the smoke of the fire, being inside, may be expelled","rationale":"Takes τοῦ πυρός with καπνός and ἐντός adverbially; attachment within the compact word order is not entirely certain."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.19","text":"By the man who helps, then, I mean the true prophet, who alone can illuminate human souls, so that we may be able to see with our own eyes the road of eternal salvation. Otherwise this is impossible, as you yourself also know, since you said a little earlier that every thesis is refuted and established, and that, depending on the ability of the person defending it, the same thesis is regarded as true and false. Thus theses no longer appear as what they are but, because of those who defend them, acquire the appearance of being or not being true or false. Because of this, the whole matter of piety had need of a true prophet, so that he might tell us realities as they are and how one must believe about everything. Accordingly, one must first test the prophet by every prophetic examination and recognize him as true; from then on, one must believe him in everything and no longer examine individually each thing said by him, but receive those things as certain—apparently by faith, yet accepted on the basis of sure judgment. For by one demonstration—the exact examination made from the beginning and from every side—all things have been grasped by sound reasoning. Therefore, before everything else, one must seek the true prophet, because without him it is impossible for human beings to have anything certain.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὸν μὲν οὖν βοηθὸν ἄνδρα","chosen":"By the man who helps, then","rationale":"Retains both the reference to a man and his assisting function."},{"source_quote":"πᾶσα ὑπόθεσις ἀνασκευάζεται καὶ κατασκευάζεται","chosen":"every thesis is refuted and established","rationale":"Uses the paired argumentative senses of dismantling and supporting a proposition."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς τὴν τοῦ ἐκδικοῦντος δύναμιν","chosen":"depending on the ability of the person defending it","rationale":"In this argumentative context ἐκδικοῦντος denotes advocating or defending a case rather than exacting vengeance."},{"source_quote":"φαντασίαν λαμβάνειν τοῦ εἶναι ἢ μὴ εἶναι ἀληθεῖς ἢ ψευδεῖς","chosen":"acquire the appearance of being or not being true or false","rationale":"Preserves the source’s full and somewhat awkward sequence of alternatives rather than simplifying its scope."},{"source_quote":"δοκούσῃ μὲν πίστει, ληφθέντα δὲ ἀσφαλεῖ κρίσει","chosen":"apparently by faith, yet accepted on the basis of sure judgment","rationale":"Maintains the contrast between apparent faith and the secure judgment established by prior examination."},{"source_quote":"βέβαιόν τι προσεῖναι ἀνθρώποις","chosen":"for human beings to have anything certain","rationale":"Expresses προσεῖναι as something certain being present or available to people."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.20","text":"And likewise he set my mind at rest, explaining to me who he is and how he is found, and making him truly findable for me. Through the discussion about the prophet he showed the truth to my ears more plainly than things seen before the eyes, so that, struck with amazement, I marveled at how no one perceives the things everyone seeks, though they lie before them. But after he had written the discourse about the prophet at that man’s command, he had the volume sent to you from Caesarea of Strato, saying that he had a command from you to write down and send you, year by year, the discourses and deeds of each year. Nevertheless, on that one first day, while still only making a beginning concerning the prophet of truth, he fully assured me about everything. Then he said: “From now on, observe the debates I conduct against those on the opposing side. If I come off worse, I am not afraid that you might waver over the truth handed down to you, for I know that it was I who appeared to be defeated, not the thesis handed down to us through the prophet. Yet I hope not to have come off worse even in the discourse of examination, in the judgment of those who have understanding—I mean lovers of truth—who can recognize which arguments are persuasive, skillfully fashioned, and pleasing, and which are plain and simple, relying solely on the truth conveyed through them.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"καὶ ὁμῶς ἀνέπαυσέν με","chosen":"And likewise he set my mind at rest","rationale":"Treats the supplied ὁμῶς as an adverb of likeness and conveys the relief expressed by ἀνέπαυσέν."},{"source_quote":"τῇ τοῦ προφήτου ὁμιλίᾳ","chosen":"Through the discussion about the prophet","rationale":"The context supports taking the genitive objectively, though “through the prophet’s discourse” remains grammatically possible."},{"source_quote":"τῶν πᾶσι ζητουμένων ἔμπροσθεν κειμένων οὐδεὶς ἐνορᾷ","chosen":"no one perceives the things everyone seeks, though they lie before them","rationale":"Preserves the contrast between universal seeking and failure to discern what lies openly before people."},{"source_quote":"τὰς καθ’ ἕκαστον ἐνιαυτὸν ὁμιλίας τε καὶ πράξεις γράφοντα διαπέμπειν σοι","chosen":"to write down and send you, year by year, the discourses and deeds of each year","rationale":"Retains both the writing and sending and connects καθ’ ἕκαστον ἐνιαυτόν with the annual record."},{"source_quote":"τὸ ἧττον ἀπενέγκωμαι","chosen":"I come off worse","rationale":"Renders the idiom of carrying away the inferior result in a debate."},{"source_quote":"περὶ τῆς παραδοθείσης σοι ἀληθείας διακριθήσῃ","chosen":"you might waver over the truth handed down to you","rationale":"Here διακριθήσῃ denotes doubt or hesitation concerning the received truth."},{"source_quote":"λιτοὶ καὶ ἁπλοῖ, μόνῃ τῇ δι’ αὐτῶν ἀληθείᾳ πεποιθότες","chosen":"plain and simple, relying solely on the truth conveyed through them","rationale":"Keeps the arguments as the grammatical subject and contrasts reliance on truth with rhetorical artistry."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"πλὴν γράψας τὸν περὶ προφήτου λόγον, αὐτοῦ κελεύσαντος, ἀπὸ τῆς Καισαρείας τῆς Στράτωνος διαπεμφθῆναί σοι ἐποίησεν τὸν τόμον","issue":"In the supplied reading, the nominative γράψας naturally shares the subject of ἐποίησεν, while the genitive absolute αὐτοῦ κελεύσαντος most naturally introduces another male as commander. The surrounding first-person narrative could instead suggest that Clement wrote at the other man’s command, so the identities of the writer and commander remain uncertain. The translation follows the supplied nominative syntax rather than silently adopting the conjecture.","proposed_reading":"πλὴν γράψαντός μου τὸν περὶ προφήτου λόγον, αὐτοῦ κελεύσαντος, ἀπὸ τῆς Καισαρείας τῆς Στράτωνος διαπεμφθῆναί σοι ἐποίησεν τὸν τόμον","blocks_publication":true}]}]}
